clue.text: Right sort of cabaret with folk singer

indicators.note: a sort of cabaret is a version of it, so the letters of cabaret and folk are recast together

explanation.surface: Someone describes a right kind of nightclub show featuring a folk singer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' rearranges the two words cabaret and folk as one pool; 'with' only joins them. 'folk singer' looks like one phrase, but only 'singer' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Roberta Flack was an American soul and folk-influenced vocalist, famous for Killing Me Softly.

clue.text: English economist has programme accepted by South American city

indicators.note: something accepted by a city is taken inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro in Brazil, usually just Rio
a card is a programme of events, as at a race meeting

explanation.surface: An economist from England has a schedule welcomed by a city in South America.
explanation.walkthrough: A race card or fight card is the printed programme of events.
explanation.definitionFit: David Ricardo was the classical political economist from England, known for comparative advantage.

clue.text: China supporting offensive game

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits underneath, so it comes after

parts.note: bad as in a bad or offensive smell
Minton is a famous English make of porcelain china

explanation.surface: Fine porcelain props up a nasty sport.
explanation.walkthrough: Minton is a Staffordshire pottery firm, so its china is a byword for porcelain.
explanation.definitionFit: Badminton is a racket sport played with a shuttlecock over a high net.

clue.text: Thatcher may have used these instruments

definitions.meaning: a roof thatcher uses dried stalks of water plants such as Norfolk reed
oboes, clarinets and bassoons are woodwind sounded by vibrating tongues of cane

explanation.definitionFit: Reeds are both thatching material and a family of woodwind instruments.

clue.text: Novice has fresh fish

indicators.note: fresh suggests something made anew, so the letters are formed afresh

explanation.surface: A beginner is given fresh fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fresh' rearranges the nine letters of NOVICE HAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Anchovies are small oily fish of the herring family, often salted.

clue.text: Rare metal found with nickel in watery fluid

indicators.note: the nickel symbol is placed in the word for watery fluid

parts.note: rheum is a watery discharge from the eyes or nose
Ni is the chemical symbol for nickel

explanation.surface: A rare metal discovered alongside nickel in a runny liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhenium is element 75, among the scarcest metals in the earth's crust.

clue.text: Land not fancied by maiden

parts.note: real means actual, not imagined or fancied
M is the abbreviation for a maiden over in cricket scoring

explanation.surface: A piece of land a young woman doesn't care for.
explanation.walkthrough: A maiden in cricket is an over with no runs scored, written M on a scorecard.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm is a kingdom or domain, a land ruled over.

clue.text: What's administered by clergyman replacing his curate?

indicators.note: replacing is read as re-placing, putting the letters in new positions

explanation.surface: A vicar asks what he hands out now that he's replacing his assistant priest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replacing' rearranges the letters of HIS CURATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Holy Communion is consecrated and given out by a priest to communicants.

clue.text: Clubs with restrictions for members

definitions.meaning: golf clubs with metal heads, numbered three to nine
fetters or shackles that restrict the limbs, members meaning arms and legs

explanation.definitionFit: Irons are both golf clubs and the chains clapped on a prisoner's limbs.

clue.text: Madonna with Child in stonework

indicators.note: the child is set inside the Madonna's name

parts.note: the Madonna is the Virgin Mary
a son is a child

explanation.surface: A Madonna and Child carved in stone.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a religious sculpture of Mother and Child; 'in' places the Child inside the Madonna's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Masonry is construction from cut stone or brick laid by masons.

clue.text: Try to borrow note in prison

indicators.note: the note is placed in the word for prison

parts.note: a cage is a place of confinement
D is a musical note

explanation.surface: Someone attempts to get a loan with a note while behind bars.
explanation.definitionFit: To cadge is to scrounge or beg something, often money, with no plan to repay.

clue.text: Bodybuilder getting annoyed in Derbyshire town

parts.note: clay is the material a body is built from, as when Adam was formed from earth
cross means irritated or angry

explanation.surface: A gym fanatic gets irritated in a Derbyshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bodybuilder' suggests a gym, but read it as a material that builds a body, as a sculptor's clay. Clay Cross is a former mining town in Derbyshire, a county of the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Clay Cross is a small town in north-east Derbyshire, England.

clue.text: Sudden inspiration: start off in bad weather

indicators.note: the start of the word is taken off, removing its first letter

parts.note: a brainstorm is a sudden clever idea

explanation.surface: Someone has a bright idea and sets off in foul weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start off' removes B, the first letter of BRAINSTORM.
explanation.definitionFit: A rainstorm is heavy rain with wind, plainly bad weather.

clue.text: Crime rendering minister powerless

indicators.note: without power, so the P that stands for power in physics is removed

parts.note: a parson is a minister of the church

explanation.surface: An offence that leaves a churchman without influence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rendering' only links; P is the usual physics abbreviation for power.
explanation.definitionFit: Arson is the criminal act of deliberately setting fire to property.

clue.text: Choose one: can opener or drink dispenser

parts.note: to opt is to choose
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the opener of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Pick one: a tin-opener or a bar's spirit measure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can opener' is not the kitchen tool but the first letter of 'can'. An optic is the upside-down measuring tap on bottles in a British pub.
explanation.definitionFit: An optic is the device fixed to an inverted bottle that releases a measured shot of spirits.

clue.text: Various countries lacking common sense

indicators.note: various suggests a range of forms, so the letters take a different order

explanation.surface: A jibe that several nations have no sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Various' rearranges the letters of COUNTRIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Cretinous is an insulting word meaning stupid, devoid of good sense.

clue.text: Pregnant? From one point of view, round? Very much so!

definitions.meaning: a heavily expecting woman is big, so is in a large condition

definitions.text: From one point of view, round?
definitions.meaning: seen one way, a round shape is a big way of being
an idiom meaning greatly, to a large extent

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means hugely or greatly, and read literally it describes being large, as when expecting.

clue.text: What's said to be merry? False note somewhere in Sicily

parts.note: the old simile 'merry as a grig' names a grig, a cricket or small eel, as merry

indicators.note: a false version of the word note is an altered one, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A singer hits a wrong note at a jolly spot in Sicily.
explanation.walkthrough: The simile 'merry as a grig' supplies A GRIG; 'False' rearranges NOTE into ENTO.
explanation.definitionFit: Agrigento is a city on the south coast of Sicily, famed for its Greek temples.

clue.text: Using empty shed to trap brown bear

parts.note: with as in 'cut with a knife', meaning using

indicators.note: the outer letters trap the colour between them
an emptied word keeps only its outer letters

parts.note: tan is a light brown colour

explanation.surface: Someone uses a bare hut to catch a brown bear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' keeps only the outer letters of 'shed', and 'to trap' puts the colour between them. 'bear' is not the animal but the verb meaning endure.
explanation.definitionFit: To withstand is to endure or resist, as one can bear pressure.

clue.text: Trick with thicker lens

parts.note: a con is a swindle or trick
denser means more compact, thicker

explanation.surface: A deception involving a thicker piece of glass.
explanation.definitionFit: A condenser is a lens or lens system that concentrates light, as in a microscope or projector.

clue.text: Firm agreement

definitions.meaning: ... as an adjective meaning solid and dense

explanation.definitionFit: Compact means both closely packed and a formal contract between parties.

clue.text: Emperor having clothes brought back? About time!

indicators.note: about means going round, so the turned word surrounds the letter for time
brought back is read as turned round, reading the word backwards

parts.note: a suit is a set of clothes

explanation.surface: An emperor finally gets his outfit returned; and not before time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought back' turns SUIT into TIUS; 'About' wraps that round T.
explanation.definitionFit: Titus was Roman emperor from 79 to 81 AD, son of Vespasian.

clue.text: Get out of bed and make use of internet expert

parts.note: to surf is to browse the web
an ace is a skilled expert

explanation.surface: Rise from bed and become an online whizz.
explanation.walkthrough: To surface is to appear after sleep, as one comes up from the depths.
explanation.definitionFit: To surface, informally, is to wake and get up in the morning.

clue.text: Sharia expert in plain clothes

definitions.meaning: a Muslim legal scholar who issues rulings on Islamic law
civilian dress worn by someone, often a soldier, normally in uniform

explanation.definitionFit: A mufti is an Islamic jurist, and the word also means civilian clothes off duty.

clue.text: See 1 across
Player almost let me see runner

indicators.note: almost means not quite complete, so the final letter is lost

parts.note: an organist plays the organ
er is the hesitation sound someone makes when thinking

explanation.surface: A musician nearly lets me catch sight of an athlete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the final T of ORGANIST. 'runner' is not an athlete but someone who runs an event.
explanation.definitionFit: An organiser runs things, so a runner of an event is its organiser.

clue.text: Men aboard accommodating current group of stars

parts.note: OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers as opposed to officers
I is the physics symbol for electric current
on as in 'on the ship', aboard

explanation.surface: Sailors on a ship take on board a current, beneath a constellation.
explanation.definitionFit: Orion is a prominent constellation named after a hunter of Greek myth.

clue.text: Suitable location for hydrant in resort

indicators.note: the letter for hydrant goes in the word for resort

parts.note: Nice is a resort on the French Riviera
H is the sign marking a fire hydrant in Britain

explanation.surface: A good spot for a fire hydrant in a holiday town.
explanation.walkthrough: British fire hydrants are marked by yellow plates bearing a large H.
explanation.definitionFit: A niche is a place or role well suited to someone or something.

clue.text: Turk getting most of France in a spin

indicators.note: most of a word is all but its final letter

parts.note: Anatole France was a French novelist and Nobel laureate

indicators.note: a spin throws the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A Turkish man gets France spinning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'France' is not the country but the writer Anatole France; 'most of' cuts his first name to ANATOL, and 'spin' turns IN A into IAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Anatolia is the Asian heartland of Turkey, so a native of it is a Turk.

clue.text: Beginners in conservatoire learn about Ravel and Schumann

indicators.note: the beginners of these words are their first letters

explanation.surface: New music students study Ravel and Schumann.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Schumann' looks like Robert, but it is his wife.
explanation.definitionFit: Clara Schumann was a concert pianist and composer, wife of Robert Schumann.

clue.text: Recruits like this getting caught out

indicators.note: the caught word lies outside, around the other piece

parts.note: taken means caught or captured
so as in 'do it so', meaning in this way

explanation.surface: New recruits, like this one, getting caught out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught out' reads as the word for caught standing outside the other piece; 'getting' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: To take on staff is to hire or recruit them.

clue.text: Late change of direction when putting end to old battle

indicators.note: one compass direction letter is swapped for another

parts.note: Verdun was the great First World War battle of 1916

explanation.surface: A tardy switch of tactics as an old battle is brought to an end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change of direction' swaps the N (north) at the end of VERDUN for E (east).
explanation.definitionFit: Overdue means late, past the time it was expected.
